bullets.text: Machine Learning (ML) is a subfield of Artificial Intelligence (AI).
ML systems learn patterns from data instead of fixed rules.
Models use learned patterns to make decisions or predictions.
Models can improve over time with more data without reprogramming.
It's about teaching computers to learn from experience, like humans.
ML is ubiquitous, powering recommendations, spam filters, and virtual assistants.
Its popularity stems from access to vast amounts of data.
Modern hardware (GPUs) provides the computational power to process data efficiently.
Sophisticated algorithms extract better insights from data than older methods.
Most common type, trained using labeled data (input + correct output).
Goal: learn input-output relationships to predict new outputs.
Example: predicting house prices based on features and actual sale prices.
Regression predicts continuous values (e.g., price, temperature).
Classification predicts discrete labels or categories (e.g., spam detection).
Uses data without labeled outputs; only inputs are provided.
Goal: discover patterns, relationships, or structures in the data independently.
Clustering groups similar data points (e.g., customer segmentation).
Dimensionality reduction simplifies data with many features (e.g., PCA).
An agent learns by interacting with an environment.
Receives feedback as rewards or penalties for its decisions.
Goal: learn a policy to maximize total reward over time.
Examples: training robots to walk, game-playing AI (AlphaGo), self-driving cars.
Data quality is crucial; noisy, biased, or incomplete data harms performance.
Overfitting occurs when a model learns training data too well but fails on new data.
Ethical concerns arise from biased data leading to biased models with real-world consequences.
Understanding data, context, and impact is as important as the algorithms themselves.
Recap of ML definition, importance, three types, and challenges.
Future lectures will dive deeper into each ML type and algorithms.
Will explore real examples and practical applications of ML concepts.
